'''Casey William Hardison''' (born 1971) is an American [[chemist]] convicted in the United Kingdom in 2005 of six offences involving [[psychedelic drug]]s: three of production, two of possession, and one of exportation.<ref name="bbcsentenced">{{Cite web | title =DIY chemist jailed for 20 years | publisher =[[BBC]] | date =April 22, 2005 | url =http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/southern_counties/4474401.stm | accessdate =August 10, 2007 }}</ref><ref name="cps-report">{{Cite journal |title = R v Casey Hardison |journal = CPS Sussex Annual Report 2004-2005 |page=6 |year = 2005 |url = http://www.cps.gov.uk/publications/docs/areas/2005/ar2005sussex.pdf |accessdate = August 10, 2007  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927194057/http://www.cps.gov.uk/publications/docs/areas/2005/ar2005sussex.pdf |archive-date=27 September 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Background==
Hardison was born in [[Washington (state)|Washington state]] in the summer of 1971.<ref name="Vice2014">{{cite web|title=The Psychedelic 'Drugs Wizard' Who Ran One of England's Biggest LSD Labs|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/casey-william-hardison-psychedelic-chemist-254/|website=Vice|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 18, 2017|archive-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019063834/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/wd43v5/casey-william-hardison-psychedelic-chemist-254|url-status=live}}</ref> He is committed to the [[entheogen]]ic use of [[Psychedelic drug|psychedelic]] substances.<ref name="erowidprof">{{Cite web | title =Erowid Casey William Hardison Vault | publisher =[[Erowid]] | date =August 2, 2007 | url =http://erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey.shtml | accessdate =August 10, 2007 | archive-date =August 5, 2007 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20070805113947/https://erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey.shtml | url-status =live }}</ref>

===Research===
In 2000, the [[Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies]] published in its bulletin Hardison's "An Amateur Qualitative Study of 48 [[2C-T-7]] Subjective Bioassays." According to Hardison, 2C-T-7 is "a fairly novel entheogenic compound that has been used in a limited context as an adjunct in psychedelic psychotherapy since 1986."<ref name="mapspaper">{{Cite journal | last =Hardison | first =Casey | authorlink =Casey William Hardison | title =An Amateur Qualitative Study of 48 2C-T-7 Subjective Bioassays | journal =Bulletin of the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies | volume =10 | issue =2 | page =11 | date =Summer 2000 | url =http://www.maps.org/news-letters/v10n2/10211har.html | accessdate =August 12, 2007 | archive-date =August 5, 2007 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20070805020254/http://maps.org/news-letters/v10n2/10211har.html | url-status =live }}</ref>

===Activism===
The [[Drug Equality Alliance]], a nonprofit organization working to secure equal rights and protections for drug users, was set up by lawyer Darryl Bickler inspired by Hardison's legal arguments.<ref name="Drug Equality Alliance">{{Cite web | title =Drug Equality Alliance - Background | year =2008 | url =http://www.drugequality.org/background.htm | accessdate =August 27, 2009 | archive-date =September 4, 2009 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20090904010347/http://www.drugequality.org/background.htm | url-status =usurped }}</ref>

==Crimes==
After moving to [[Brighton]], Hardison illegally manufactured three [[Drugs controlled by the UK Misuse of Drugs Act|class A drugs]]: [[2C-B]], [[Dimethyltryptamine|DMT]], and [[LSD]].<ref name="localpaper"/> Having set up a laboratory in his rented bungalow,<ref name="localpaper">{{Cite news |last =Cridland |first =Ali |title = Drugs wizard gets 20 years |page =1 |publisher =Brighton Argus |date =January 21, 2005 |url=http://www.brightoncity.com/martyrdom.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060513130442/http://www.brightoncity.com/martyrdom.html |archive-date=13 May 2006 |url-status=dead}}</ref> he used £38,386 worth of chemical ingredients to produce hallucinogenic tablets with a street value of up to £5m.<ref name="bbcguilt">{{Cite web | title =DIY chemist guilty of making drug | publisher =[[BBC]] | date =March 18, 2005 | url =http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/southern_counties/4362841.stm | accessdate =August 12, 2007 | archive-date =January 22, 2022 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20220122012440/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/southern_counties/4362841.stm | url-status =live }}</ref>

===Arrest===
In July 2003, Hardison sent two packages to the U.S. During a random inspection at the FedEx hub in Memphis, Tennessee,<ref name="Court of Appeal" /> officials found four bags of [[MDMA]] (Ecstasy) hidden between pages of a magazine. MDMA is a [[psychoactive drug]] used primarily as a [[recreational drug use|recreational drug]] at parties and raves.<ref name="localpaper"/><ref name="bbcguilt" /> Thus alerted, British authorities monitored Hardison until arresting him near Brighton in February 2004.<ref name="bbcguilt" />

===Legal proceedings===
The case was complicated by the involvement of U.S. law enforcement agents, some of whom attended the trial as witnesses. Hardison represented himself in court.<ref name="cps-report" />

====Pre-trial arguments====
Hardison challenged the drug laws as violating his [[cognitive liberty]] and his rights to [[freedom of thought]], therapy and religion,<ref name="erowidprof"/> contending that his basic [[human rights]] and [[liberties]] were violated by his arrest, detention and prosecution. In response, the judge of the [[Crown Court]] wrote, "I have come to the sure and clear conclusion that Mr. Hardison's arguments are misconceived and I reject each and every one of the Human Rights arguments."<ref name="Crown Court Judgment">{{Cite journal | title = R v Casey Hardison | journal = HMCS Lewes Crown Court | date = Jan 2005 | url = http://erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey_2005_jan_crown_court_judgement1.pdf | accessdate = August 27, 2009 | archive-date = February 5, 2009 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090205092228/http://www.erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey_2005_jan_crown_court_judgement1.pdf | url-status = live }}</ref>

====Trial and conviction====
In March 2005, after a 10-week trial at [[Lewes Crown Court]],<ref name="Court of Appeal" /> the jury found Hardison guilty. Calling him a "dangerous individual," the judge said Hardison was motivated by greed and set up his ‘illegal’ drug factory<ref name="bbcsentenced" />—which a chemist from the [[Forensic Science Service]] called the most complex laboratory he had ever encountered<ref name="Court of Appeal" />—in the UK because U.S. drug laws were "too hot." The court was told Hardison's father used proceeds of his son's crimes to buy a yacht.<ref name="bbcsentenced" />

====Sentence====
In April 2005, Hardison was sentenced to twenty years imprisonment in the UK with a recommendation that he be deported upon his release.<ref name="cps-report" /><ref name="localpaper" />

====Appeals====
In May 2006, the [[Court of Appeal of England and Wales]] rejected Hardison's first application for leave to appeal, finding that none of his grounds had sufficient merit. In his decision, Justice Keith wrote that Hardison's criminal enterprise "was not an amateurish operation in a garden shed. It was a careful and calculated attempt to introduce new synthetic drugs onto the UK market which could have reaped great financial rewards."<ref name="Court of Appeal">{{Cite journal | title = R v Casey Hardison | journal = HMCS Court of Appeal of England and Wales | date = May 25, 2006 | url = http://www.bailii.org/cgi-bin/markup.cgi?doc=/ew/cases/EWCA/Crim/2006/1502.html&query=r+and+v+and+hardison&method=boolean | format = [[PDF]] | accessdate = August 27, 2009 | archive-date = January 22, 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220122012403/http://www.bailii.org/cgi-bin/markup.cgi?doc=%2Few%2Fcases%2FEWCA%2FCrim%2F2006%2F1502.html&query=r+and+v+and+hardison&method=boolean | url-status = live }}</ref>

Subsequently, the [[House of Lords]] (then the [[court of last resort]] for UK criminal law) refused Hardison's final appeal, and his similar appeal to the [[European Court of Human Rights]] likewise failed.<ref name="erowidprof"/>

===Prison life===
Hardison found drugs readily available in prison. "LSD, 2C-B, DMT, pharmahuasca, research chemicals, kratom, cannabis, home-brewed alcohol—I did a whole bunch of shit in there," he told ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]'' in 2014. "Drugs are more available in prison than they would be for the common man trying to find them on the street. And the British prison system is fairly gentle—it's pretty damn civilized."<ref name="Vice2014"/>

===Release===
Following his release from prison in May 2013,<ref name="erowidprof"/> Hardison was deported from the UK to the U.S.<ref name="Vice2014"/> After living in [[Victor, Idaho]],<ref name=" VictorMan">{{Cite news|author=Thorne, Ryan|url=http://www.mtexpress.com/news/cops_courts/victor-man-pleads-not-guilty-to-felony-drug-charges/article_f0ce3216-159a-11e7-bd0c-47f2b554baac.html|title=Victor man pleads not guilty to felony drug charges|newspaper=Idaho Mountain Express|date=March 31, 2017|access-date=May 18, 2017|archive-date=June 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629154223/http://www.mtexpress.com/news/cops_courts/victor-man-pleads-not-guilty-to-felony-drug-charges/article_f0ce3216-159a-11e7-bd0c-47f2b554baac.html|url-status=live}}</ref> he moved to Northern California.<ref name="ChargesDropped">{{Cite news|author=Murdock, Joshua|url=http://www.mtexpress.com/news/cops_courts/charges-dropped-in-alleged-drug-bust/article_b0b744ae-999a-11e7-b4d0-b732c230b493.html|title=Charges dropped in alleged drug bust|newspaper=Idaho Mountain Express|date=September 15, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017|archive-date=September 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915164949/http://www.mtexpress.com/news/cops_courts/charges-dropped-in-alleged-drug-bust/article_b0b744ae-999a-11e7-b4d0-b732c230b493.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Post-incarceration==
===Death of Anthony Birkholz===
On January 17, 2017, in [[Jackson Hole]], [[Wyoming]], after drinking heavily, Hardison and two other men consumed a substance believed by the [[Teton County, Wyoming]] coroner to be the psychedelic drug [[5-MeO-DMT]].<ref name="Buckrail05-18-2010">{{cite web|title=Coroner's Inquest rules death of Birkholz accidental but possibly preventable|url=http://buckrail.com/coroners-inquest-rules-death-of-birkholz-accidental-but-possibly-preventable/|website=Buckrail|date=May 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017|archive-date=October 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018070854/http://buckrail.com/coroners-inquest-rules-death-of-birkholz-accidental-but-possibly-preventable/|url-status=live}}</ref> One of the men, artist and filmmaker Anthony Birkholz,<ref name="MemorialCash">{{Cite news|author=Mieure, Emily|url=http://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/memorial-cash-confiscated-by-police/article_d9bd93d2-e0e2-5a58-b58d-b27a2cbc2145.html|title=Memorial cash confiscated by police|newspaper=Jackson Hole News&Guide|date=June 7, 2017|access-date=November 23, 2017|archive-date=January 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122012417/https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/memorial-cash-confiscated-by-police/article_d9bd93d2-e0e2-5a58-b58d-b27a2cbc2145.html|url-status=live}}</ref> died from aspiration of [[vomiting|vomitus]] secondary to food, alcohol and 5-MeO-DMT ingestion. The jury at the coroner's inquest found that Birkholz's death was accidental but could have been prevented.<ref name="Buckrail05-18-2010"/><ref name="GlossedOver">{{Cite news|author=Chambers, Jessica Sell|url=http://planetjh.com/2017/05/31/the-buzz-2-usual-suspect/|title=In Birkholz death, alcohol, drug abuse were largely glossed over|newspaper=Planet Jackson Hole|date=May 31, 2017|access-date=July 25, 2017|archive-date=August 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808114257/http://planetjh.com/2017/05/31/the-buzz-2-usual-suspect/|url-status=live}}</ref> Hardison called [[5-MeO-DMT]] "a very rare, beautiful experience," but admitted he hadn't done any since the night Birkholz died. "Looking back now," he said, "I'm not so charmed."<ref name="Inquest">{{Cite news|author=Mieure, Emily|url=http://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/inquest-death-wasn-t-natural/article_1e3e3d66-83ef-58f2-8053-93d7b144732c.html/|title=Inquest: Death wasn't natural|newspaper=Jackson Hole News&Guide|date=May 24, 2017|access-date=July 25, 2017|archive-date=June 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170615092252/http://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/inquest-death-wasn-t-natural/article_1e3e3d66-83ef-58f2-8053-93d7b144732c.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Aftermath ====
A day after Birkholz's death, Hardison launched a [[GoFundMe]] page, "Tony Birkholz Slips the Mortal Coil," raising $6,100.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} "This campaign," Hardison wrote, "intends to raise memorial funds and to ensure his remains reach his intended destination. Any remaining funds will be donated to the Buffalo Field Campaign, West Yellowstone, Montana, in the fight to protect the last remaining wild buffalo." After several hundred people attended a vigil at the Pink Garter,<ref name="MemorialCash" /> a music venue and cocktail lounge in [[Jackson, Wyoming]],<ref name="PinkGarter">{{cite web|title=Cocktails & Creatives|url=http://www.pinkgartertheatre.com/event/1580721-cocktails-creatives-jackson-hole/|website=Pink Garter Theatre|access-date=October 18, 2017|archive-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019004820/http://www.pinkgartertheatre.com/event/1580721-cocktails-creatives-jackson-hole/|url-status=live}}</ref> Hardison said part of the $6,100 raised online paid for the open bar that night. None of the remaining $3,900, however, was immediately donated as pledged to the Buffalo Field Campaign.

===== Arrest in Idaho =====
In February 2017, Hardison was stopped in [[Bellevue, Idaho]], for speeding. After a drug-sniffing dog detected controlled drugs, police searched Hardison's vehicle. They found $7,928 in cash, about two pounds (≈ 0.9&nbsp;kg) of marijuana, a half gram of cocaine and what was believed to be [[heroin]]. However, tests by the [[Idaho State Police]] labs determined that the suspected substance was not heroin.<ref name="VictorMan" /> Hardison admitted that half of the $7,928 in cash was the missing GoFundMe money collected to honor Tony Birkholz.<ref name="MemorialCash" /> On March 21, Hardison pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from the traffic stop.<ref name="VictorMan" />

In June 2017, a member of Birkholz's family filed a complaint with the [[FBI]]'s [[Internet Crime Complaint Center]] accusing Hardison of fraud.<ref name="MemorialCash" /> The $3,900 donation to the Buffalo Field Campaign in honor of Anthony Birkholz was finally made in September 2020.<ref name="MyUser_Https:_September_23_2020c">{{cite web |title=Teton County inmate challenging state drug laws |date=September 23, 2020 |url=https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/teton-county-inmate-challenging-state-drug-laws/article_2872632d-7c0a-51d7-9ae8-7cf5425e660d.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924132437/https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/teton-county-inmate-challenging-state-drug-laws/article_2872632d-7c0a-51d7-9ae8-7cf5425e660d.html |archive-date=September 24, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref>

In August 2017, all charges against Hardison, including three felony counts and one misdemeanor, were dismissed after a judge ruled that the traffic stop was unconstitutionally delayed without reasonable suspicion, allowing a canine officer time to detect the presence of controlled substances.<ref name="ChargesDropped"/>

===Attempted arrest in Wyoming===
According to the ''Jackson Hole News & Guide'', on August 6, 2018, police attempted to arrest Hardison for selling a large quantity of marijuana to an undercover officer. However, Hardison eluded them after a high-speed chase.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cops say drug suspect eluded them in chase|url=https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/article_54b12225-6e9f-5983-84c5-0983d58c93c1.html|website=jhnewsand guide.com|date=August 8, 2018|access-date=August 8, 2018|archive-date=August 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808172050/https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/article_54b12225-6e9f-5983-84c5-0983d58c93c1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Arrest in California===
On July 28, 2020, Hardison was arrested in Yorkville, CA, by the Mendocino County Sheriff's Office. A $500,000 Fugitive From Justice warrant saw Hardison extradited back to Jackson, to face charges stemming from the botched sting operation by Wyoming officers.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.gillettenewsrecord.com/news/wyoming/article_98700269-5d4b-5533-bd6f-588b50822487.html |title=Returned Jackson fugitive to represent self |newspaper=[[Gillette News Record]] |agency=Wyoming News Exchange |date=September 1, 2020 |access-date=October 24, 2020 |archive-date=October 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027121444/https://www.gillettenewsrecord.com/news/wyoming/article_98700269-5d4b-5533-bd6f-588b50822487.html |url-status=live}}</ref> On November 17, 2020, in his defense, Hardison planned to present a motion to Dismiss the Indictment based on the premise that the Wyoming Controlled Substances Act, W.S. § 35-7-1001 et seq., ("the Act") violates his due process and equal protection rights guaranteed by the Wyoming Constitution and the Constitution for the United States of America.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey_2020_oct_motion_to_dismiss.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=November 5, 2020 |archive-date=November 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116190532/https://erowid.org/culture/characters/hardison_casey/hardison_casey_2020_oct_motion_to_dismiss.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Arrest in Black Rock City, Nevada===
On September 2, 2024, Hardison was arrested at the annual [[Burning Man]] festival by the [[Pershing County, Nevada|Pershing County]] Sheriff's Office for Sexual Assault, Arrest on Other-Agency Warrant, and for Possession of Scheduled (1) or (2) C/S LT 14 Grams, 1st or 2nd Offense. The Arrest on Other-Agency Warrant was due to an outstanding warrant related to the prior Wyoming charges, after Casey again left the Jackson Hole area before his legal situation was resolved.<ref>{{Cite news|author=Osei-Tutu, Demetria|url=https://www.themirror.com/entertainment/music/gallery/inside-burning-man-2024-mugshots-674380 |title=Burning Man 2024 mugshots: Inside all of the arrests of the 2024 festival |newspaper=[[The Mirror US News]] |agency=a Reach plc subsidiary |date=September 3, 2024 |access-date=September 4, 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|author=O'Toole, Scarlett|url=https://www.themirror.com/entertainment/celebrity-news/burning-man-festival-man-arrested-675288 |title=Man arrested on final day of Burning Man Festival for sexual assault and drug possession |newspaper=[[The Mirror US News]] |agency=a Reach plc subsidiary |date=September 3, 2024 |access-date=September 4, 2024 }}</ref>

===2024 presidential campaign===
In a January 22, 2021 interview with the ''[[Jackson Hole News&Guide]]'', Casey Hardison announced his 2024 bid for president. Before he slipped underground again, Hardison had planned to run for President in the forthcoming general election as a candidate for a revived [[Democratic-Republican Party]], originally founded by [[Thomas Jefferson]] and [[James Madison]] in 1792.<ref>{{cite web|title=Casey Hardison is presidential hopeful Felonies do not disqualify candidate who aims to restart party defunct since the 1820s.|url=https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/casey-hardison-is-presidential-hopeful/article_9934e283-e186-5e25-82ce-9918e3e281f7.html|website=jhnewsand guide.com|date=February 3, 2021|access-date=February 3, 2021|archive-date=February 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210203154553/https://www.jhnewsandguide.com/news/cops_courts/casey-hardison-is-presidential-hopeful/article_9934e283-e186-5e25-82ce-9918e3e281f7.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Hardison has appeared on the [[television show]]s ''[[Hamilton's Pharmacopeia]]''<ref name="Morris2016-S01E06">{{cite episode | credits = [[Hamilton Morris|Morris H]] | date = 7 December 2016 | title = The Lazy Lizard School of Hedonism | series = [[Hamilton's Pharmacopeia]] | season = 1 | number = 6 | url = https://vimeo.com/546752807| publisher = [[Vice Media]] | network = [[Viceland]]}}</ref> and ''[[Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller]]''.<ref name="PsychedelicTimes2024">{{cite web | title=Psychedelic Timeline | website=Psychedelic Times | date=21 October 2024 | url=https://psychedelictimes.com/psychedelic-timeline/ | access-date=6 July 2025 | quote = Trafficked: LSD premieres on Vice TV. Mariana van Zeller interviews a manufacturer of ergotamine tartrate and Casey Hardison in her search for an active manufacturer of LSD.}}</ref>
